h: Soft Play Survival Guide for Grown-Ups
p: Big soft play centres are brilliant for kids, but a little strategy helps the adults come out the other side still smiling. Pick a base table early with a clear view of the main frame, so you can see little ones coming and going. Set a simple meeting point for older children, especially in a large centre where kids can disappear into tunnels for ages.

Dress for the job too. You may well end up crawling through a tunnel to rescue a stuck toddler or coax a nervous one down a slide, so comfy clothes and socks for yourself are a good idea. Pop drinks bottles with lids in your bag, and take a spare top for the kids, as soft play and sweaty foreheads go hand in hand.

Planning soft play around naps and mealtimes makes a big difference. A session straight after lunch can mean a happy, energetic hour followed by a lovely sleepy drive home. Arrive hungry and you'll be fighting a losing battle within twenty minutes.

Chatelherault Country Park in Hamilton is a great contrast to an indoor play session. It's built around a grand 18th-century hunting lodge and has woodland trails along the Avon Gorge, plus play areas of its own. Closer to hand, Strathclyde Country Park's loch-side paths are flat and pushchair-friendly, perfect for a run around on bikes or scooters. Mixing indoor play with an outdoor walk is often the secret to a day that ends with tired, happy kids rather than overexcited ones.
